age.evidence: weighting from 280 to 350 g (age of 120-180 PND)

sex.evidence: Male Wistar-Han rats (Charles River, Sulzfeld, Germany)

dosing.evidence: animals received subcutaneous ( sc ) single injections of 25B-NBOMe dissolved in 0.9% NaCl at five doses of 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg
LSD was injected ip at a dose of 0.1 mg/kg

handling.evidence: Paper does not describe handling protocol

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12-h light/dark cycle (the light was switched on at 6 a.m.)

assays.assay_description: Head and body twitches (wet dog shakes) counted by an experienced blinded observer immediately after injection for 240 min; scores summed across 12 observation periods.

application_type.evidence: 25B-NBOMe administered s.c.; LSD administered i.p. at 0.1 mg/kg as reference

setup_habituation.evidence: No mention of pre-test apparatus habituation

setup_restrain.evidence: behavior defined as rapid shaking of the head, neck, and trunk... observed during 240-min observation period

food_restriction.evidence: Standard observation cage; no food in apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: Standard observation cage; no water in apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: counted immediately after drug injection during 240-min observation period

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe induced head and body twitches (WDS) in rats in an inverted U-shaped dose-response manner, with 0.3 mg/kg most potent and other doses (0.1, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg) weaker but still significant. LSD (0.1 mg/kg) was nearly equally potent as the highest 25B-NBOMe dose.
outcomes.evidence: 25B-NBOMe induced head and body twitches (WDS) in rats... The dose of 0.3 mg/kg produced the most potent effect (Fig. 5). The effect of 0.1, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg doses was weaker but significant (F 6,49 = 127, p < 0.0001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The number of episodes counted for 240 min

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Results were expressed as an average of sum values of all episodes during the observation time

B4_ethological.evidence: WDS/HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours by rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: counted by an experienced observer who was blind to the treatments

E1_environment_type.evidence: Observation cage (standard apparatus for WDS counting)

D1_continuity.evidence: 240-min observation period starting immediately after injection

assays.assay_description: Wooden closed square arena (60×60×40 cm); introductory session (5 min, 2 identical objects) followed by recognition session (5 min, one object replaced with novel) with 30 min inter-session interval. Animals pre-familiarized to arena 24 h before. Co-administration with scopolamine in some groups.

application_type.evidence: 25B-NBOMe (0.3 and 3 mg/kg, sc); scopolamine i.p. as adjunct

setup_habituation.evidence: Each animal was familiarized with the arena (pre-test, without any object) 24 h before the testing day

time_to_assay.evidence: The introductory session was performed 20 min after injection of a drug

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe (3 mg/kg) lowered the recognition index vs control, indicating impaired short-term memory; 0.3 mg/kg had no effect. Scopolamine (1 mg/kg) reversed the 25B-NBOMe-induced decrease in Ri.
outcomes.evidence: There was a significant difference in the Ri between animals treated with the higher dose of 25B-NBOMe and the control group (Fig. 6b; F 2,23 = 139, p < 0.0001). Importantly, the Ri in the control and low-dose 25B-NBOMe-treated group reached ca. 72% and 68%, respectively, while in the 25B-NBOMe 3 mg/kg group, it was 45%.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Exploration time for familiar and novel objects, and recognition index

B4_ethological.evidence: Exploration of an object was defined as follows: licking, sniffing, or touching the object

B6_cognitive.evidence: Novel object recognition test requires recognition memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Exploration time was measured using a digital laboratory timer by two independent observers

E1_environment_type.evidence: wooden closed square arena with painted black walls (60×60×40 cm)

E3_bedding.evidence: Not reported; arena cleaned after each session implies bare floor

D1_continuity.evidence: The NOR test consisted of two sessions: introductory and recognition one (5 min each) with a 30 min inter-session interval

D3_recording_days.evidence: Both sessions on testing day; pre-familiarization day had no data collected

D4_baseline.evidence: Pre-familiarization without data collection; no pre-drug baseline reported

assays.assay_description: Round black arena (1 m diameter) virtually divided into 8 sections; behavior recorded for 10 min starting 30 min after injection. Measures: time of walking, number of line crossings, episodes of peeping under arena, grooming events, rearings. Some groups co-treated with scopolamine.

application_type.evidence: Rats were placed in the middle of the arena 30 min after 25B-NBOMe subcutaneous injection

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test apparatus habituation described for OF

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals free to move in arena

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe dose-dependently decreased locomotor activity: reduced walking time, line crossings, and peeping episodes. No rearing or grooming was observed in treated animals. Scopolamine alone increased walking and crossing but did not reverse 25B-NBOMe-induced decreases.
outcomes.evidence: 25B-NBOMe decreased the time of walking (F 2,19 = 134, p < 0.0001) and the number of episodes of crossing (F 2,19 = 110, p < 0.0001) and peeping (F 2,19 = 32, p < 0.0001) in a dose-dependent manner

B1_num_measures.evidence: time of walking, number of line crossings, episodes of peeping under the arena, number of events of grooming, and number of rearings

B4_ethological.evidence: number of events of grooming, and number of rearings

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Manual observation; no automated classifier described

E1_environment_type.evidence: round black arena (1 m in diameter)

E6_spatial.evidence: Round arena virtually divided into 8 sections

assays.assay_description: Med Associates Seamless Open Field Arena (43×43×30 cm) divided by dark insert into light and dark compartments connected by a hole. Rats placed in dark compartment 20 min after injection and allowed to explore freely for 15 min. Measured: time in dark/light, immobility, ambulatory distance, vertical activity, stereotypical activity, via infrared beam-break (Activity Monitor).

application_type.evidence: 25B-NBOMe administered subcutaneously; rat placed in dark compartment 20 min after injection

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test habituation to LDB apparatus described

setup_restrain.evidence: was allowed to explore freely for 15 min

time_to_assay.evidence: The rat was placed in the dark compartment 20 min after injection of a drug

outcomes.summary: 25B-NBOMe (3 mg/kg) significantly prolonged time spent in the dark zone and decreased time in the light zone compared to control, indicating an anxiogenic effect. Both doses (0.3 and 3 mg/kg) significantly decreased ambulatory distance, vertical activity, and stereotypical activity in both zones.
outcomes.statistics: U=0, p<0.001 (dark zone time vs control at 3 mg/kg); U=0, p<0.001 (light zone time at 3 mg/kg); multiple U=0, p<0.001 for activity measures
outcomes.evidence: the time was longer and statistically significant in the rats treated with 25B-NBOMe at the dose of 3 mg/kg as compared to control (U=0, p<0.001). Accordingly, the time spent by all animals in the light zone was shorter and was decreased in the 25B-NBOMe 3 mg/kg group in comparison to control

B1_num_measures.evidence: immobility time, ambulatory distance, vertical activity time, stereotypical activity time, and the time spent in the dark and light compartment

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone time and activity counts; no natural-repertoire behaviour scored

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates Activity Monitor (infrared beam-break) — position/activity tracking only

E1_environment_type.evidence: Seamless Open Field Arenas for rats (43×43×30 cm)

E2_shelter.evidence: A dark insert was used to divide the chamber into two equally sized compartments: a light compartment and a dark compartment

E6_spatial.evidence: divide the chamber into two equally sized compartments... A hole in the insert enabled rats to move freely between compartments

D1_continuity.evidence: allowed to explore freely for 15 min

judge_notes: Excluded microdialysis (neurochemistry) and comet assay (genotoxicity) as non-behavioural endpoints per rubric.
Four distinct behavioural assays retained: WDS, NOR, OF, LDB. Both candidates agreed on these.
NOR scored as Multiple discrete sessions (D1=1) because introductory and recognition sessions are separately recorded with a 30-min interval on the same day — followed glm candidate.
OF B1 scored 2 (4–6 measures: walking, crossings, peeping, grooming, rearing) — followed qwen since 5 measures were explicitly reported even if some had zero values.
WDS application_type set to 'multiple' to capture LSD i.p. reference; 25B-NBOMe was s.c.
B7 set to 0 for LDB even though Med Associates Activity Monitor was used, because beam-break systems are explicitly listed as score 0 per rubric.
B4 for NOR scored Yes because sniffing/licking object exploration is an ethological act explicitly defined; B4 for OF scored Yes because grooming and rearing are listed as measured behaviours.
